title: Life Data Types
description: Shared schema for captured life evidence (audio recordings, transcripts, screen activity), the conversations derived from it, and the facts and entities taken from those conversations, across the Ushadow ecosystem. All times are absolute UTC so evidence from different recordings and devices can be lined up. Evidence is never overwritten: a correction is a new record.

TimeRange.title: TimeRange
TimeRange.description: An absolute UTC interval. end must not be before start.

CaptureSource.title: CaptureSource
CaptureSource.description: A device or channel that produces evidence, e.g. an Omi pendant, a phone microphone, or a desktop screen recorder.

modalities.description: What this source captures. audio_input is a microphone; audio_output is system audio (always media, never the owner speaking).

Speaker.title: Speaker
Speaker.description: A voice heard in one recording. label is local to that recording: 'Speaker 0' in two recordings may be different people. personId is set only once voice recognition or a human has identified who it is.

label.description: Diarization label, unique within the recording

personId.description: Stable identity across recordings, if known

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description: One line of transcript: contiguous speech from one speaker, delimited by speaker change or pause. The atomic unit of a recording.

Recording.title: Recording
Recording.description: One continuous piece of captured audio. A recording is how the audio was cut (silence, button press, disconnect, file size), not what happened. One conversation can span several recordings, and one recording can hold parts of several conversations. range is the absolute bounds of the audio; startReason and endReason say why each edge is where it is. The words are in Transcript: one recording can have several.

contentHash.description: Hash of the audio content, used to detect the same audio stored twice

currentTranscriptRevision.description: Transcript.revision to use by default. Older revisions are kept.

AudioRef.title: AudioRef
AudioRef.description: Where the audio of one recording is stored. It is a pointer only: removing it (an erase, or a pruned file) leaves the rest of the Recording as it was. The hash of the audio is Recording.contentHash.

uri.description: Location of the audio file, e.g. 's3://example-bucket/audio/rec-a.opus'

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description: One reading of a recording by a transcription model. A transcript is never overwritten: a better model or new speaker labels make a new revision. The one exception is a provisional revision (a live transcript that grows while the recording is still being made): it may be replaced in place until a final revision of the recording exists, and is frozen after that. Segment ids are only stable within one revision, so other types point at a time range of the recording, not at segment ids.

recordingId.description: Recording.id this is a reading of

revision.description: Identifies this version, unique within the recording

speakers.description: Every speaker label used by segments

TranscriptCorrection.title: TranscriptCorrection
TranscriptCorrection.description: A human fix to what a recording says, for one time range: the right words, the right speaker, or both. It is applied on top of every transcript revision, so a new transcription does not undo it.

text.description: The correct words for the range

speakerLabel.description: The correct Speaker.label for the range

personId.description: The correct person for the range, if known

EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef
EvidenceRef.description: A pointer to proof: a time range of one recording. The range is the anchor and stays valid for every transcript revision. quote is the exact words read from transcriptRevision, kept for display and for re-checking after a new transcription.

transcriptRevision.description: Transcript.revision the quote was read from

CutReason.title: CutReason
CutReason.description: Why a recording edge is where it is. Edges caused by silence, file_boundary, disconnect or size_limit are often not the end of a real conversation.

Fragment.title: Fragment
Fragment.description: A run of consecutive speech in one recording about one subject. A recording that changes subject without a pause yields several fragments. range is the anchor: it stays valid when the recording is transcribed again. segmentIds is optional and only valid for transcriptRevision.

transcriptRevision.description: Transcript.revision the segment ids refer to

segmentIds.description: Consecutive segment ids in transcriptRevision, in order. Optional.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what was said

SpeakerRef.title: SpeakerRef
SpeakerRef.description: Points to one speaker label in one recording.

Participant.title: Participant
Participant.description: One person in a conversation. Because speaker labels are local to a recording, the same person may appear as 'Speaker 0' in one recording and 'Speaker 1' in the next; speakerRefs records every label that is this person.

personId.description: Stable identity across conversations, if known

speakerRefs.description: Every recording-local label that is this participant

ConversationPart.title: ConversationPart
ConversationPart.description: The part of one recording that belongs to a conversation. The time between consecutive parts is a pause in the conversation.

Thread.title: Thread
Thread.description: A subject that runs through a conversation, possibly with interruptions. Its fragments need not be consecutive and may come from different recordings of the same conversation.

participantIds.description: Participant.id values from the same conversation

Conversation.title: Conversation
Conversation.description: A time-bounded exchange between people. It can contain pauses, so it is made of one or more parts, each claiming an interval of a recording. Recordings are referenced, not copied. range runs from the start of the first part to the end of the last part, pauses included.

revision.description: Starts at 1. Goes up each time late evidence, a correction or a new Link changes the conversation. The id stays the same.

closedAt.description: When the conversation was closed (UTC). Not set while it is still open.

citations.description: Proof for the claims in title and summary

parts.description: Recording intervals in chronological order; gaps between them are pauses

participants.description: Everyone heard, including media and background voices with their role

fragmentIds.description: Fragments inside the parts, in chronological order

threads.description: Subjects that recur within the conversation

screenObservationIds.description: Screen activity that overlapped the conversation, as context

meetingId.description: MeetingMarker.id, when a meeting app defined the bounds

entityRefs.description: People, projects, tasks, places and organisations the conversation is about

FrameRef.title: FrameRef
FrameRef.description: A pointer to one screen frame. The capture device keeps the full frame store and may prune it, so a frame can stop being available.

frameId.description: Identifier in the capture device's frame store

mediaUri.description: Where the uploaded copy is stored

ScreenSample.title: ScreenSample
ScreenSample.description: A snapshot of what was on screen at one moment inside an observation. frame is the frame the sample came from, if any.

ScreenObservation.title: ScreenObservation
ScreenObservation.description: A period of continuous screen context: one application, window and URL, from switch-in to switch-out. Like a recording, it is a capture unit, not an event: one observation can hold several activities (two game matches) and one activity can span several observations. range runs from switch-in to switch-out.

appName.description: Focused application, if known (some windows report none)

url.description: Browser URL, when the app is a browser

frames.description: Candidate frames spread across the observation, for choosing a representative image

representativeFrameId.description: FrameRef.frameId chosen to represent the observation

MeetingMarker.title: MeetingMarker
MeetingMarker.description: A meeting detected from a machine signal (a meeting app holding the microphone, a calendar entry). The strongest evidence of where a conversation starts and ends.

title.description: Meeting title, if the app or calendar provides one

CaptureGap.title: CaptureGap
CaptureGap.description: An interval when a source recorded nothing. Distinguishes 'nothing was captured' from 'captured, but nothing happened'.

recordingId.description: Recording.id the gap is inside, e.g. a range erased from one recording. Not set: the gap is between recordings.

Link.title: Link
Link.description: A decided relation between two items (recordings, fragments, observations or conversations), or a decided cut inside one recording (split_at). Storing the decision lets a later run reuse it instead of deciding again: a run looks up key first. A Link is never changed. To override one, add a new Link whose retracts is the old id. A human Link wins over a rule or model Link.

toId.description: Later item id. Not set for split_at.

at.description: split_at only: the time of the cut (UTC)

key.description: Identity of the question that was decided, e.g. a hash of kind, fromId, toId or at, and policyVersion. Two Links with the same key answer the same question.

policyVersion.description: Version of the rules or prompt that decided it

model.description: Model that decided it, when decidedBy is model

gapSeconds.description: Time between the end of fromId and the start of toId; negative when they overlap

EntityKind.title: EntityKind
EntityKind.description: What kind of thing an entity is

Entity.title: Entity
Entity.description: A person, project, task, place or organisation that conversations and facts are about. 'These two names are the same entity' is a Fact with key same_entity, not an edit of this record.

aliases.description: Other names for the same entity

confirmed.description: false for a bystander: no profile is kept until the user confirms the entity

EntityRef.title: EntityRef
EntityRef.description: Points to one entity, with enough to show it without a lookup.

FactSource.title: FactSource
FactSource.description: Who said so. person: a human. agent: a model. sensor: a rule or a capture system. Same meaning as Decider: human = person, model = agent, rule = sensor.

Direction.title: Direction
Direction.description: For a promise: who owes whom, seen from the owner

Sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
Sensitivity.description: How private the content is. Used to decide which agents may read it.

FactSubject.title: FactSubject
FactSubject.description: What a fact is about: one entity, task or conversation.

FactValue.title: FactValue
FactValue.description: The content of a fact. The named fields are the shared ones; a key may add its own.

evidence.description: Proof. Required in practice when source is agent.

due.description: When it is due: a date or a date-time (ISO 8601)

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description: Something that was said or done, kept for ever. Same shape as a taskfacts fact (ushadow_facts). A fact is never changed and has no status: whether it still counts is worked out from retractions and newer facts. key says what happened, as a thing plus a past verb (task_requested, promise_made, decision_made, constraint_added, preference_stated, question_opened, done_reported, same_entity, correction, forget, erased). It never names a status.

occurredAt.description: When it was said or done in the world (UTC). For speech, the recording time.

scope.description: Who can see it. Not set: everyone the owner allows.

retracts.description: Fact.id of a fact that was wrong

CaptureBundle.title: CaptureBundle
CaptureBundle.description: Evidence, derived structure and facts for one time span (for example one local day), with every item referenced by id.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to define the span, e.g. 'Europe/London'

ownerPersonId.description: Whose capture this is: the personId of the owner (the person with Speaker role owner)

SourceKind.title: SourceKind
SourceKind.description: What kind of device or channel produces the evidence

Modality.title: Modality
Modality.description: What a source captures. audio_input is a microphone; audio_output is system audio (always media, never the owner speaking).

SpeakerRole.title: SpeakerRole
SpeakerRole.description: owner: the person wearing or using the device. participant: someone talking with them. media: TV, radio, video, podcast. background: nearby speech not addressed to the owner. unknown: not decided.

RecordingOrigin.title: RecordingOrigin
RecordingOrigin.description: live: streamed as it happened. recovered: downloaded later from device storage. upload: a file the user added. import: a historical backfill.

FrameAvailability.title: FrameAvailability
FrameAvailability.description: local: only on the capture device. uploaded: a copy is stored centrally (see mediaUri). pruned: no longer available anywhere.

TextSource.title: TextSource
TextSource.description: accessibility text is structured and reliable; ocr is a fallback for windows without an accessibility tree

ScreenState.title: ScreenState
ScreenState.description: What the user was doing with the screen

TranscriptStatus.title: TranscriptStatus
TranscriptStatus.description: provisional: a live draft that may still change and may be replaced in place. final: complete; never changed. Not set means final.

GapCause.title: GapCause
GapCause.description: Why nothing was captured. excluded means the user chose not to keep it, including a range the user erased later.

LinkKind.title: LinkKind
LinkKind.description: continues: toId carries on the same conversation or activity after a pause or cut. duplicate_of: toId is the same capture stored again. overlaps: both captured the same moment from different sources (e.g. phone and pendant). unrelated: checked, and not the same event. split_at: fromId is a recording that holds the end of one conversation and the start of the next; the cut is at Link.at.

Decider.title: Decider
Decider.description: Who made the decision. A human decision is never overwritten by a rule or model.
